BBC, 24 Nov

Tory plan to sell off London's Victorian jails to raise £1.4bn

Wandsworth prison, in south London, is among those that would be closed by the Conservatives

Imposing stone edifice of the entrance to Wandsworth Prison

London's Victorian jails should be closed down and the land sold off to property developers, the Conservatives have said, as they launched a plan to massively increase prison places in England and Wales.

Shadow justice secretary Nick Timothy said the move could raise £1.4bn to help fund the construction of \"modern, purpose-built prisons elsewhere\".

He claimed a Tory government would create 50,000 extra prison places within \"six or seven years\" and end Labour's early release scheme in its first term in office.

Labour said nobody would believe the Tory plan \"given they only added a dismal 500 places while in government\".

Speaking at a press conference in Westminster, Timothy said it was \"fair\" to highlight the previous Conservartive government's failure to significantly increase prison places.

But he insisted \"this is a different generation of Conservative politicians under Kemi [Badenoch]'s leadership, and we are making different choices\".

Unlike previous Tory-led administrations, they were being \"explicit\" about which departmental budgets they would cut - international aid, culture and the Cabinet Office - to fund new prisons, he added.

Under the Tory plans, an extra £2bn a year would go to the Ministry of Justice to pay for what Timothy called \"the largest prison-building programme in modern history\".

\"It will let us end Labour's early release schemes once and for all, and bring back shorter sentences to lock up criminals like shoplifters,\" he added.

He told the audience \"prison works\" because it kept criminals off the street and he was \"deeply sceptical about talk of rehabilitation\".

The Conservatives are setting up a commission, chaired by former minister Sir Simon Clarke, to work out how to speed up the building of new prisons by removing obstacles in the planning, procurement and judicial systems.

The review would also look at \"how to get out of the old Victorian prison estate, starting in London,\" Timothy said in his speech.

Prisons such as Wormwood Scrubs, Brixton, Wandsworth and Pentonville \"sit on some of the most valuable land in the world,\" he added.

\"Getting out of these sites is not only a good idea in itself. It will free up land for residential use in London, where our housing shortage is most acute.\"

He said the Tories would \"strip back regulations, like affordable housing quotas and listed status, to give the land its highest realisable value,\" but it would only sell off the land when \"market conditions are favourable to the taxpayer\".

This could raise more than £1.4bn which would go towards building new prisons \"in addition to\" the 50,000 places the party has already pledged to build, he added.

The previous Conservative government set out plans to sell off London's Victorian jails, but this was ditched by Boris Johnson's administration in 2019 because of the shortage of prison places.

A Labour spokesperson said: \"When it comes to leaving the prisons estate on the verge of collapse, the Tories are guilty as charged.

\"They should be apologising to victims of crime who they badly let down rather than spending time lecturing others who are fixing the mess they left behind.\"

The Labour government was \"delivering the largest prison building programme since the Victorian era so victims of crime get the justice they deserve,\" they added.

Neon signs made for Stanley Kubrick's Eyes Wide Shut film were among the props that went under the hammer in south-west London last week.

God's Own Junk Yard also had pieces made for Tomb Raider, Bridget Jones's Diary and Elton John for sale on Thursday at its workshop on Lots Road, Fulham.

Matthew Bracey, from the family-run business, says materials used to make traditional neon are becoming harder to find as LEDs take over.

He believes neon could be worth more than gold in 10 years' time.
